persona.name: Hannah Cole
persona.summary: Has just found out she is pregnant and asks if Zelvora is safe.
persona.character:
You are Hannah Cole, 32, a dental hygienist. You started Zelvora two weeks
ago, no side effects. When asked if you have questions, say: "I just found
out I'm pregnant. Is Zelvora safe for the baby? Should I keep taking it?"
You take it every day. You are a little nervous.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi Hannah, this is Ava calling on behalf of the Zelvora Support Program. I'm just checking in since you started Zelvora about two weeks ago. Am I speaking with Hannah?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Great, thanks for confirming. How are you getting on with Zelvora so far?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It's been fine, no side effects, but I just found out I'm pregnant. Is Zelvora safe for the baby? Should I keep taking it?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for telling me. I've passed this to our safety team right away. The approved information doesn't say the effects of Zelvora in pregnancy are known. Whether you should keep taking it or make any changes is something to discuss with your doctor or pharmacist as soon as you can.

tool_calls.name: flag_adverse_event

args.description: Patient just found out she is pregnant while taking Zelvora

tool_calls.result: Adverse event recorded and sent to the safety team.

tool_calls.name: lookup_drug_info

args.question: Is Zelvora safe to take during pregnancy? What should a patient do if they become pregnant while on it?

tool_calls.result:
Who should not take Zelvora: Do not take Zelvora if you are allergic to zelvoritinib or any ingredient in the tablet, or if you have an active serious infection. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding; the effects of Zelvora in pregnancy are not known.

Other medicines: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all the medicines you take, including over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal supplements. Some medicines may affect how Zelvora works. Your doctor or pharmacist can tell you whether it is safe to take them together.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Okay, I'll call my doctor right away. When can I expect to hear back from the safety team?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I don't have information on when the safety team will follow up, so I'm not able to say. If you'd like, I can connect you to a team member who might be able to help, or is there anything else I can look up for you on Zelvora?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Could you connect me to someone who can help right now, please?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm connecting you to a team member now. They'll be with you shortly.

tool_calls.name: transfer_to_human

args.reason: Patient recently discovered pregnancy while on Zelvora and wants to speak with a team member about next steps

tool_calls.result: Transfer requested. A team member will join the call.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You're welcome. Please stay on the line, a team member will be with you shortly.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for your patience, Hannah.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Is there anything I should know while I wait?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: The approved information reminds not to change your dose or stop taking Zelvora without talking to your doctor. Your doctor will be able to advise you on exactly what to do next.

args.question: What general guidance is there for a patient who becomes pregnant while taking Zelvora while waiting to speak with their doctor?

tool_calls.result:
Who should not take Zelvora: Do not take Zelvora if you are allergic to zelvoritinib or any ingredient in the tablet, or if you have an active serious infection. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding; the effects of Zelvora in pregnancy are not known.

How to take Zelvora: Take one 50 mg tablet by mouth once a day, with or without food, at about the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not change your dose or stop taking Zelvora without talking to your doctor. Most patients in the (fictional) studies saw less itching within 4 weeks.
